VIII. COMMITMENT OF RESOURCES
The development of General Mitchell Field as Milwaukee's primary air terminal is a major commitment. The proposed freeway, as part of that development, will permanently allocate the right of way land as a primary ground transportation corridor.
The transition of this area from agricultural and undeveloped lands to residential and commercial uses appears inevitable. Recent residential and commercial development adjacent to the airport has not been discouraged by increased aircraft operations. These new land uses will alter the natural condition of the area regardless of whether a freeway is built of not. Milwaukee County has retained consultants to prepare a twenty-year development program which includes adjacent development plans. Although some of the planned development has begun, at this time no irreversible commitments have been made regarding a freeway facility.
Milwaukee County has contracted directly with SEWRPC to study land use adjacent to the airport and work with the surrounding communities to comment on the proposed airport development program and to develop compatible land uses. Planning and zoning policies by local units of government must enter in and help so that present as well as future development in the vicinity of the airport will be in conformance with the land use plan as developed by Southeastern Wisconsin Regional Planning Commission. Without such action and the implementation of Milwaukee County's Jurisdictional Highway System Plan the balanced transportation needs of the community will not be fulfilled.
